newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss sight deposits fall to 3,772.9 million Sfr.
newsitem.headline: Swiss sight deposits fall to 3,772.9 million Sfr.

text.p: The Swiss National Bank said sight deposits fell by 553.9 million Swiss francs to 3.77 billion in the reporting period ended May 30.
Statement of June 2 in millions of Swiss francs:
Borrowing at the emergency Lombard window fell by 7.5 million francs to 2.3 million in the reporting period.
Outstanding borrowing via the discount facility and swaps of money market certificates fell by 168.7 million francs to 1,598.7 million.
An SNB spokesman said the decline in sight deposits in the latest week was not a sign of a more restrictive SNB policy but rather reflected low demand for liquidity.
The spokesman said the decline in sight deposits did not mean the SNB has become more restrictive.
"It doesn't have anything to do with that," he said.
"In the market there is a lot of money, it was enough for the banks. The bank demand was not very high. But we are still very committed to keeping the market liquid," the spokesman said.
